summary: Provisioned API token binding mismatch causes scheduled webhook 403s in private deployment
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-11 22:30 UTC DataViz Labs' scheduled ingestion job started receiving 403 responses when calling the Redwood admin endpoint to upload model artifacts. Impact: scheduled webhooks fail and ingestion backlog is growing; customer reports ~100 failed calls/hour. This is a private (on-prem/VPC) deployment.

Observed behavior: Calls from the customer's scheduled worker use a long-lived provisioned API token. Requests reach the private control plane but are rejected with 403 and the admin-api logs show a token binding lookup failure (token appears valid, but the binding key wasn't found). No 5xxs on our side. Customer did a tenant aliasing change in their IdP around the same time (enabled short tenant aliasing for SCIM provisioning).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In a private deployment with tenant-scoped provisioning, create a service-account and provision an API token via SCIM/IdP sync.
2) Configure a scheduled worker to use the provisioned token to call POST /v1/admin/models/upload on the private control plane.
3) Trigger the scheduled job or run it manually; observe 403 responses returned to the caller while control plane request logs show TOKEN_BINDING_NOT_FOUND entries.

4) Re-provisioning a new token with the same service account succeeds if created via Console (manual flow), but tokens created by SCIM provisioning continue to fail until the token is rotated manually via Console.
logs: 2026-03-11T22:31:02Z admin-api ERROR request_id=5f3a2f token=<redacted> result=403 reason=TOKEN_BINDING_NOT_FOUND tenant="td-97f" expected_key="tenant-97f"
Request headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>; X-Tenant-ID: td-97f; X-Forwarded-Proto: https
SCIM sync log (customer-idp): provisioning user/serviceAccount(serviceAccount-42) -> tenantAlias=td-97f canonicalTenantId=tenant-97f
investigation_notes: Support reproduced a failing call in our private staging by simulating SCIM-created tokens where the 'tenant_alias' field differs from the 'canonical_tenant_id' stored in token-store.

Hypothesis: SCIM provisioning (customer IdP) started writing 'tenant_alias' into the token metadata and our token-store lookup path prioritizes the canonicalTenantId key. When tokens are minted by the customer's SCIM flow they contain tenant_alias but token-store index keys used by admin-api expect the canonicalTenantId; lookup fails and we treat token as unbound.

Confirmed: tokens created via Console (manual) include canonicalTenantId and succeed. Tokens created via SCIM include only tenant_alias; we did not add an alias->canonical reverse mapping in the token-store index during provisioning, leading to a missed binding lookup.

Cross-checks: looked at SCIM audit (customer) and found the tenant_alias toggle was enabled 2026-03-11 22:12 UTC (matches incident start). No recent changes in admin-api code or token-store index schema on our side.
Severity assessed as Sev1 due to steady failure rate and growing ingestion backlog.
comments: Aisha Khan (Support): Customer reports ingestion failures after enabling 'short tenant alias' in their IdP. Asked for confirmation of the time window and sample token. Waiting on token dump (redacted) from customer.

Customer (DataViz Labs): Provided redacted token metadata and SCIM audit log showing tenantAlias=td-97f canonicalTenant=tenant-97f. They confirm Console-created tokens work but SCIM-created ones do not.

Ethan Liu (SRE): Reproduced in private staging. Short-term workaround is to re-provision tokens via Console or to add alias mapping into token-store for affected tenants. Creating INT follow-up to add alias reconciliation job.
Engineering (Auth): Adding linked PR to accept tenant_alias in token binding lookup for tokens created by SCIM (soft-fail fallback) — will be behind feature flag for controlled rollout.
resolution:
Workaround applied: added temporary alias mapping for tenant 'td-97f' -> 'tenant-97f' in the customer's token-store; rotated affected SCIM-provisioned tokens. Customer verified scheduled jobs resumed and backlog cleared within 25 minutes.

Permanent fix: engineering merged a change to try tenant_alias when canonical lookup fails and to emit a reconciliation warning. Patch PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/4821. Plan: roll out feature-flagged fix to private control plane clusters week of 2026-03-15, then enable reconciliation job to backfill aliases for recently provisioned tokens.

Follow-ups: INT-12045 (create periodic alias reconciliation job), Confluence runbook updated with SCIM provisioning checklist. Customer notified and will keep ticket open for 48h monitoring.
